newsitem.title: USA: Nevada Energy president calls charges "frivolous".
newsitem.headline: Nevada Energy president calls charges "frivolous".

text.p: Nevada Energy Co Inc President Stefan Tevis on Wednesday said statements in a lawsuit alleging that company directors misappropriated assets were "frivolous, libelous and totally without merit."
In a statement made available to Reuters by Nevada Energy, the company said it has not been served with the lawsuit and learned of it from a Reuters news report on Monday.

The lawsuit was filed in the Delaware Chancery Court last week by two former directors of Nevada Energy, Michael Kassouff and Richard Cascarilla. In September, Cascarilla was replaced as its secretary-treasurer and general counsel.
The plaintiffs seek unspecified damages against Tevis and the current Nevada board on behalf of Nevada Energy, a nominal defendant.

According to court papers, the defendants allegedly diverted "approximately $1.2 million in Nevada Energy's funds for non-corporate purposes." The suit also alleges the defendants usurped a business opportunity intended for Nevada and breached their duty of loyalty to Nevada by ignoring "illegal sales" of common stock. They also are alleged to have allowed the conversion of "preferred stock into common stock at an artificially depressed price."

In its statement Wednesday, Nevada Energy said it would "vigorously defend any such action and does not presently believe such disgruntled employee litigation would have any adverse material affect on the company."
"NEC continues to pursue its financing and growth plans in the energy and telecommunications areas and...plans further substantial cquisitions in communications related areas," Tevis said.

In May, Waterford Trust Co, an Irish corporation, took control of Nevada Energy for $5 million in equity financing and replaced the incumbent board with Waterford directors. Nevada Energy Controller Ken Bowers told Reuters that Waterford was "a group of private European investors."
Nevada Energy recently relocated its headquarters from Reno, Nevada, to Santa Barbara, California.
